questions.stem: The Family Discount Card costs \(\$60\) per year. For a family of \(2\) adults (\(\$15\) each) and \(3\) children (\(\$8\) each), one cinema trip costs \(\$54\) normally or \(\$36\) with the card. How many times in the same year must they go to the cinema before they start to save money on the cost of the card?
questions.hint: Find how much they save per trip ($54 - $36 = $18). Divide the $60 card cost by $18 (3.33... trips) and round UP to the next whole trip!

keyPoints.note: Total savings must strictly EXCEED the $60 card cost.

steps.explain: Calculate the savings on each cinema trip: \(\$54 - \$36 = \$18\) saved per trip.

steps.explain: Divide the \(\$60\) card cost by \(\$18\) per trip: \(60 \div 18 = 3\dfrac{1}{3}\) trips.
Check \(3\) trips: \(3 \times \$18 = \$54 < \$60\) (not yet saving). Check \(4\) trips: \(4 \times \$18 = \$72 > \$60\) (net saving of \(\$12\)).
Therefore, they must go \(4\) times in the same year to start saving money.
